item.title: The release of predatory bugs Orius laevigatus and Orius strigicollis (Heteroptera: Anthocoridae) against Frankliniella occidentalis on santpaulias in the Peter the Great Botanical Garden
item.description: The predatory anthocorids Orius laevigatus and O. strigicollis were released against the Western flower thrips on Saintpaulia spp. in a greenhouse. In the winter-spring period, the thrips population decreased to 0.1 thrips per flower, and the biological efficiency was 94 and 96 % when O. laevigatus and O. strigicollis were used, respectively. item.title: New records of the emerald ash borer Agrilus planipennis Fairmaire (Coleoptera: Buprestidae) in the southern European Russia
item.description: The emerald ash borer Agrilus planipennis Fairmaire (Coleoptera: Buprestidae) is a dangerous invasive pest of ashes, Fraxinus spp. Based on the results of a survey conducted in July 2025, the first record of A. planipennis in the Karachay-Cherkess Republic is reported, new foci were detected in Stavropol Territory (Mineralnye Vody region), and the locations of foci were clarified in Krasnodar Territory, including the first record of the pest in urban plantings in the city of Krasnodar. item.title: First record of Pammene blockiana (Lepidoptera: Tortricidae) in Russia
item.description: The study reports the first record of the tortricid moth Pammene blockiana from Russia. Its males were captured in Sochi in May 2025 in pheromone traps baited with the synthetic sex pheromone of the quarantine pest, the Oriental fruit moth Grapholita molesta. A total of 48 males of P. blockiana were collected from seven traps deployed in gardens and ornamental tree plantings in Sochi. item.title: Prospects for using the entomopathogenic fungus Akanthomyces muscarius to protect tomatoes from pests and diseases
item.description: This study assessed the efficacy of the entomopathogenic fungus Akanthomyces muscarius against the greenhouse whitefly Trialeurodes vaporariorum and the gray mold pathogen Botrytis cinerea. It was found that the area of B. cinerea infestation on tomato leaves was reduced after pre-treatment with conidia of two out of three A. muscarius strains. item.title: Assessment of antibiotic resistance in Erwinia rhapontici, the causal agent of pink grain of cereals
item.description: The opportunistic bacterium Erwinia rhapontici causes pink bacteriosis of wheat and rye grain, significantly reducing the quality of grain products and limiting grain export. Isolation of pure bacterial culture is necessary for effective diagnostics, required for disease prevention. Presence of E. rhapontici in infected plants as a part of bacterial complex, requires selective factors, such as antibiotics. item.title: Black point in wheat: reality vs stereotypes
item.description: The “black point “ symptom is a common discoloration of wheat and barley grain observed in most regions worldwide where these crops are grown. There are strict standards for the content of black point grains in batches of food wheat both in Russia and abroad. The mechanisms involved in the appearance of dark pigment have not yet been fully elucidated. item.title: Fungi associated with sunflower and their significance as pathogens in Russia
item.description: Despite the considerable attention devoted to the study of sunflower diseases, inaccuracies in the names of diseases, assessments of their practical importance, and the use of scientific names of pathogens are still frequently encountered in the literature. This leads to confusion and reduces the informativeness of published data on the phytosanitary situation. item.title: Tilletia fungi on wheat: biological and ecological features, distribution and harmfulness
item.description: Smut fungi of the genus Tilletia are widespread and harmful pathogens of wheat all over the world. In the last decade, due to the expansion of organic farming zones, there has been an increase in their importance, which determines the need for increased attention to this problem. A review of the literature data on fungi of the genus Tilletia (T. caries, T. laevis, T. controversa), pathogens of common and dwarf bunt of wheat is presented.
